chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah from Isḥāq ibn Muḥammad al-Nakhāʿī said:

Al-Fahfāḥī asked Abū Muḥammad (peace be upon him): 'What is the matter with the poor, weak woman that she takes one share while the man takes two?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, upon the woman there is no jihad (military striving) and no nafakah (financial maintenance) and no maʿqūlah (blood money/compensation), for that is upon the men.'

So I said to myself: 'It had been told to me that Ibn Abi al-ʿAwjāʾ asked Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) about this matter and he answered him with this answer.' So Abū Muḥammad (peace be upon him) turned to me and said: 'Yes, this is the question of Ibn Abi al-ʿAwjāʾ, and the answer from us is one; if the meaning of the question is one, our last one follows the same as our first one, and our first and our last are equal in knowledge, and to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) is their excellence.'
ai.seo_question: Why do women inherit half the share of men in Islamic law according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Al-Fahhākī queries Imām al-Ḥasan al-ʿAskarī (peace be upon him) regarding the female inheritance share, receiving the explanation that women are exempt from the financial burdens of jihad, nafakah, and maʿqūlah, which rest upon men. The Imām confirms this ruling's consistency with earlier Imams, noting that their knowledge is equal and derived from the Prophet and ʿAlī, thereby establishing a continuous, unified jurisprudential tradition (tawātur) within the Shia school.
